why: Fill each '?' day with an hour count from 0 to day_hours so the total hits work_hours exactly: a bounded-composition generator. Backtrack day by day, trying digits in increasing order so results come out already sorted.
hints: Subtract the fixed digits from work_hours first: you need to spread the remaining hours over the '?' days, each between 0 and day_hours.

Recurse over the '?' positions left to right, trying 0, 1, ..., day_hours. Because the positions are fixed and digits are tried in ascending order, the finished strings are produced in lexicographic order.
Prune: stop if the hours left go negative or exceed (days left) x day_hours. With at most 7 slots and 9 digits the search is tiny.
pitfalls: Only the '?' days are limited by day_hours; the given digits are kept as they are, even if larger.
Remaining hours can be 0: then every '?' becomes 0 and there is exactly one schedule.
Return the strings in ascending order; build each by replacing only the '?' positions.
constraints:
• 1 <= work_hours <= 56
  • 1 <= day_hours <= 8
  • |pattern| = 7
  • Each character of pattern is a digit 0..8 or '?'.
  • There is at least one correct schedule.
